RagShortTexts: The Vlandia competition horse is the standard mount of the Knights of the Banner, with amazing impact.

Variants.Content: The Rodeo is the standard mount of the Banner Knights of Vlandia and one of Calradia's most famous warhorses. They are huge and powerful, making them almost unstoppable when charging on flat ground. However, this extreme impact also sacrifices some speed and flexibility, especially when climbing hills. But overall, it is still a very good war horse.

Show horses are the pride of our Vlandia. It may not be as fast as a prairie horse, and it may be a little cumbersome when climbing hills, but its value has never been in racing. When the flag knights mount a group charge on the plains on competitive horses, the power of crushing everything is enough to make any enemy tremble. A good competition horse is a moving fortress.

A competitive horse is a horse that needs to make use of its strengths and avoid its weaknesses. On flat ground, it was invincible, and no cavalry could compete with it in a frontal charge. But if you let it chase Khuzait's horse archers, or let it cross the mountains, it will really be difficult for it. A wise commander will use the rodeo horse where it is most appropriate rather than complain about its shortcomings.

The knight I serve rides a rodeo horse. Usually in the camp, it is so slow that someone has to come down to hold it up the slope. We all laugh at it privately. But once on the battlefield, when it rushes up with the knight on its back, you will know that those shortcomings are worth it. It will crash directly into the enemy's formation, and neither spears nor shields can stop it. In that moment, you forget all about its clumsiness.

It goes without saying that competitive horses are good horses. But it’s not suitable for us civilians – it’s too expensive, doesn’t run fast, and is not suitable for long-distance travel. It was born for war, and its value can only be reflected in the crotch of a knight. For those of us doing business, it is more practical to choose a horse with a fast pace.

I gave someone a rodeo horse as a gift. Walking on the road was slow, and the slopes were even worse. I almost missed the deadline. But later I heard that the horse carried its owner and defeated an infantry phalanx on the battlefield, and the knight was promoted. Since then I have understood that some horses are not used to drive, but to determine victory or defeat.

Vlandia’s competitive horse is a war horse with obvious advantages and disadvantages. Its impact is indeed unparalleled. On the plains, even our armored cavalry had to avoid its edge. But its speed and endurance are somewhat inferior. Once the terrain becomes complicated, its power will be greatly reduced. The war horses of our empire may not have such extreme impact, but they are better in balance.

Anyone who has ever played against a competitive horse knows how powerful it is. On flat ground, their charge was as powerful as a landslide. But we also figured out its weakness - don't take their charge head on on the plains. Lure them to slopes and woodlands, and their power will be halved. This is basic common sense when dealing with Vlandia cavalry.

According to the records of "Calradia Customs", competitive horses are the product of cross-breeding between ancient imperial war horses and Vlandia forest horses. Its breeding direction is extremely focused on impact, resulting in relatively weak speed and endurance. It is an "extreme" war horse. Under suitable battlefield conditions, it is almost invincible; but in unfavorable terrain, it is easily restrained.

It is a fact that competitive horses are not useful in the desert. They are too heavy, tend to get trapped in the sand, and are extremely slow when climbing dunes. But on the plains of Vlandia they make formidable opponents indeed. We Aserai don't look down on it just because it doesn't do well in the desert - we just try not to fight it on the plains.

The competitive horse is the overlord on the southern plains, but when it comes to the ice fields and snow in the north, its impact power cannot be exerted. Our warriors rely more on their legs and shield wall. Still, if we were to one day face off against the Vlandians on the plains, I'd also like to have a team of allies on rodeo horses by my side.

Rodeo horses don’t thrive in the woodlands, which is the luck of us Battania people. If they could charge in the forest like they do on the plains, we would have been unable to stop them. We respect its strength as a war horse, but we are also grateful that our home is not a plain.

Competitive horses have strong impact, but they cannot run fast or far. On the steppe our mounted archer could easily keep his distance and he could not overtake us. But we wouldn’t be foolish enough to collide head-on with a team of charging rodeo horses. Each type of horse has its own strengths, and a smart warrior knows how to take advantage of his own strengths and avoid those of his enemies.

A competitive horse is a good fighting horse, but it is not easy to use in all situations. If you are a mercenary cavalry in Vlandia, riding this will take your charge power to a new level. But if you are a lone ranger who wants to travel around, its slow speed will make you waste a lot of time on the road. Which horse to choose depends on what you want to do.

The competitive horse is the core pillar of Vlandia’s military system and is also a highly specialized war horse. Its advantages and disadvantages are equally outstanding: it has the best impact of the Calradia, but at the expense of speed, endurance and terrain adaptability. This "extreme" breeding idea determines the dominance of the Vlandia army on the plains, and also determines their limitations in complex terrain. When evaluating a competitive horse, you cannot separate it from the context in which it is used.
